drivers.driver: Management's current plan of partial, phased divestitures is an inadequate response to the persistent mispricing and margin underperformance versus peers [D03, D06].
The window for the annual-meeting cycle provides a critical governance lever to hold the board accountable for shareholder returns [D03, D07].
The company trades at a significant discount to likely reserve NAV, which is best unlocked through a full sale rather than continued operational drift [D02, D04].

final.memo:
Pogo Producing Company remains a textbook case of a valuable resource base obscured by poor capital allocation and ineffective governance. While management has initiated a divestiture program, these half-measures are insufficient to close the valuation gap; they serve only to delay the inevitable conclusion that this franchise should be sold in its entirety [D03, D07]. The market continues to discount these assets, reflecting the lack of confidence in management's ability to drive sustainable operating returns [D01, D06].

We have been patient, but our thesis—that the sum of the parts far exceeds the trading value—is being eroded by continued reinvestment and the costs of delay [D02, D07]. A partial asset sale is not an end in itself; it is the moment to demand a formal strategic review and a full sale process [D03]. We will not wait for the market to eventually 'figure it out' while our capital is tied up in a business that is clearly not maximizing value for its owners [D05, D08].

With the annual meeting cycle approaching, the time for private engagement has passed. We are escalating our position to publicly advocate for the only outcome that makes sense: a clean break and a sale of the company to a strategic buyer who can manage these assets with the scale and focus they require [D03, D07]. We expect the board to immediately engage with representatives of the shareholders to implement this change [D07].
